approach: Add `check_job_size(reading)` as one new `step!` in `refusing_check` (crates/athena-core/src/reading/checks.rs), second, right after `check_prior_result_and_scope`. The check has two parts. (1) Group rule: map each deliverable other than CHANGELOG.md to one of four groups: `config` (athena.toml or defaults.toml, via the existing `CONFIG_FILES`), `ci` (`.github/`), `docs` (`docs/` and root `*.md`) and `code` (everything else: crates, xtask, Cargo files, studies). Refuse a reading that spans more than 3 groups, which means all four. Plainly: this part refuses only a reading that spans all four groups. Both failed jobs (20261025-183644-t67q, 20261017-205554-zaj2) span all four. I read HISTORY.txt: no landed commit in the 200 spans all four (the most is 3). (2) Count backstop: refuse above 30 non-changelog deliverables. I recounted: exactly 2 of 200 landed commits exceed it, 9a97e24 (48 paths) and 6e7fd3a (31 paths other than CHANGELOG.md, lines 779-811; a grep for a commit header followed by 31 or more path lines matched two commits). Commit paths stand in for deliverables, so these figures are estimates. The declared share is kept at the accepted criterion 5 text, 'expected 6% of newly refused readings, an estimate and not a measurement'. It is not changed. The doc comment and CHANGELOG name the complements, so the check is not read as a full size bound: the forecast-based `check_reading_size` (reading.rs:330, which trusts the reader's own wall-time median) and a later producer no-change guard (out of scope, a follow-up). Study readings and readings with a question are skipped, as in `check_scope_limit`. No prompt, config or workflow file changes; the refusal text carries the repair.

decisions.choice: Measure size as the number of separable surface groups (docs, config, ci, code) with bound 3, plus a count backstop of 30 non-changelog deliverables. Both are named constants `MAX_JOB_GROUPS` and `MAX_JOB_DELIVERABLES`. The doc comment and CHANGELOG state the rule plainly: the group part refuses only a reading that spans all four groups; the backstop refuses above 30 deliverables (2 of 200 landed commits in HISTORY.txt: 9a97e24 with 48 paths and 6e7fd3a with 31); `check_reading_size` and a later producer no-change guard are the complements.
decisions.reason: HISTORY.txt shows the only measure that separates the two failed jobs from landed work is spanning all four groups. Count alone separates nothing below 31. The groups are the 'separable surfaces' both introspections propose splitting on. Reusing `CONFIG_FILES` (checks.rs:577) keeps one definition of a config file. Answers finding 3: the rule is described as what it is, one conjunction plus a high backstop, and the text names the complements.

rejected.option: Refuse above 8 deliverables or 4 surfaces (crate, docs, xtask, .github, root each a surface)
rejected.why: HISTORY.txt shows many landed commits above 8 paths (97d1e5c 13, d6d2ad1 15, dd4d76d 12, f2d168c 21, 823dd32 about 27) and 5 to 8 surfaces (dd4d76d, 69057b9). It would refuse ordinary landed jobs.

rejected.option: Count the reader's criteria or request words
rejected.why: A proxy; the deliverable list is the real measure.
It refuses 14 or more landed commits and still misses a small job crossing four groups (the t67q shape, 9 paths).

rejected.option: Treat xtask or docs as separate groups (up to 5)
rejected.why: 6f1b5f1 and several other landed commits would reach 4 groups. xtask is Rust code, so it is part of `code`.

rejected.option: Move the backstop above 31 to spare 6e7fd3a
rejected.why: Needs 48 to clear both, which makes the backstop nearly inert. 30 is round, refuses 2 of 200 (1%), and fits inside the declared share.

decisions.choice: Keep the declared share exactly as the accepted criterion 5 states it: 'expected 6% of newly refused readings, an estimate and not a measurement'. The doc comment, CHANGELOG item and tests all carry 6%, and the test asserts `share == Some(6)`.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 1. A planner cannot edit an accepted criterion. `replay_declaration_of(reading)` calls `replay_declaration(&reading.acceptance_criteria, ..)` (replay.rs:289-290), so the replay holds the candidate against 6% + 5 points = 11%, and the text of the code and CHANGELOG matches the criterion. 6% covers the evidence: the two known failed jobs are at most 2 of the 50 readings in the replay window (4%), and the backstop adds 1% of landed commits. The '4% plus 5 gives 9%' reasoning is deleted. 6% is below the 25% threshold, so no reason text is needed (replay.rs:165).

rejected.why: Conflicts with accepted criterion 5 and with the replay, which reads the share from the reading.
Both failed jobs would be refused if they sit in the replay window.

decisions.choice: A directory deliverable gets its group from its first path component (`crates/athena-core/src/` is code). A root directory deliverable (`.`, `./`, empty) counts as all four groups.
decisions.reason: The group rule does not depend on how many files a path stands for, so a directory cannot hide size. The only way to claim every group in one path is the root, which is made to count as all of them.

rejected.option: Count a directory as the bound's worth of files
rejected.why: It would refuse any reading that lists a directory such as `crates/athena-cli/tests/`, which landed commits touch.

decisions.choice: Skip readings whose capability is not `change` or that carry a question, as `check_scope_limit` does (checks.rs:706). Place `step!(check_job_size(reading));` second, after `check_prior_result_and_scope`.
decisions.reason: A study reading has no change to measure, and a reading with a question has no accepted scope. A reading that must be split makes later repairs moot, so it is refused first. The retry check stays first because it needs the earlier attempt. The adjacency tests pin survey to history_fixture, outcome_state to environment_reach, governance to outcome_state and environment_reach to defined_terms, not this position.

rejected.why: The reader would first repair scope-limit text in a reading that is then refused for size, costing a read round.

decisions.choice: The producer no-change guard stays out of scope; the refusal text states the repair.
decisions.reason: The brief puts run/producer.rs and run/send_back.rs out of scope, and the gate acts before dispatch, so no producer run is spent.

rejected.why: It acts after the run is spent and is out of scope.

risks.risk: The group rule is calibrated on two failed jobs and 200 landed commits. It refuses only a reading that spans all four groups. A large job spanning three groups (for example config, ci and code with 25 files) is not refused, and the backstop does not reach it either. The check is not a full size bound.
risks.mitigation: The doc comment and CHANGELOG item state this plainly and name the complements: the forecast-based `check_reading_size` and a later producer no-change guard. The two bounds are named constants, so a later change is one line, and the at-the-bound tests move with it.

risks.risk: Commit paths in HISTORY.txt stand in for reading deliverables, so the 0-of-200 (groups) and 2-of-200 (count) figures are estimates, and landed commits are survivors that cannot show three-group jobs fit one run.
risks.mitigation: The CHANGELOG item, doc comment and criterion label the figures an estimate and not a measurement. The verification replay over the last 50 accepted readings measures the real share and holds the candidate above the declared 6% plus 5 points.

risks.risk: An existing test reading is refused: it spans four groups or has more than 30 deliverables.
risks.mitigation: I searched readings with long deliverable lists in reading.rs, refusal_corpus.rs, steward.rs, run/tests.rs and drain.rs and found none above 3 paths. Criterion 6 runs the whole suite, and a failure names the reading. The fix is to shrink the fixture, never to raise the bound.

risks.risk: A reader retried after the refusal still lists all four groups and is refused again.
risks.mitigation: The error tells the reader to keep one dependency-ordered group and name the others in `out_of_scope`, which existing checks accept. `read_for` re-reads once with the refusal text. Automatic splitting stays out of scope.

risks.risk: Path forms are misclassified: `./` prefixes, directory deliverables, root files such as README.md or Cargo.lock, `studies/`, `xtask/shard-timings.txt`.
risks.mitigation: `job_groups` normalizes with `normalized_path` (checks.rs:775) first. athena.toml and defaults.toml map to config, a path under `.github/` to ci, `docs/` and any other root `.md` file to docs, and all else to code. `.`, `./` and empty map to all four groups. `job_size_bound_is_general` has a case for each form.
